claim: PUM 10.5.2: is fold-and-cut the discrete analogue of unitary evolution? (unitary gate = bijective + norm-preserving)
verdict: NOT a unitary gate: the mirror fold is NOT injective (400 angle collisions -- theta and 2TH-theta both land on the same radius, e.g. theta=10.0 and theta=30.0 both give r=10.00), so it has no well-defined inverse (2 preimages of a generic mid-branch point), and the folded path does not preserve the development's arc length (L_fold/L_dev = 0.504, not 1).  Unitarity requires a bijective norm-preserving map; the fold is a many-to-one projection that re-scales the metric content.
